findings: The November 7, 2026 capture adds a two-link index at the PAYCO South Korea acceptance URL (new raw 1–12). The matched May 8, 2026 capture documents those two variants (old raw 1–8 and 105–107). Diff line 300 joins the prior final sentence and first new link. Compare the preserved originals at old raw 296–298 and new raw 11–12.

The dated Checkout guidance describes 28 merchant locations including Singapore, South Korean buyers, KRW presentment and all line items, and Checkout payment mode with setup and subscription mode unavailable. Dynamic presentation and manual selection are alternative Checkout configurations. Keep the 100 KRW minimum, no card-passthrough maximum and separate 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up ceiling (old raw 10–46). The separate Direct API creates and confirms a PaymentIntent using server-supplied client secret and browser confirmation (old raw 115–149 and 218–276).

The mapped summary retains the basic routes but overgeneralizes the sample omissions, leaves the NICEPAY disclosure scope and test/outcome transitions unclear, and omits the visible browser error-reference discrepancy (source 13–36; old raw 128–145 and 218–286).

The separately captured `2026-07-29.dahlia` changelog adds `payment_method_options.payco.setup_future_usage=none` on applicable Checkout Session and PaymentIntent surfaces to indicate PAYCO will not be saved (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-samsung-pay-and-payco-setup-future-usage-none-only-2026-11-07.md:5-21). A no-save option does not document PAYCO reuse or Checkout setup/subscription mode. The November Korea overview independently lists PAYCO one-time only (raw/stripe-payments-countries-korea-2026-11-07.md:154-164). Qualify the distinction at source lines 13 and 20 and the reciprocal Korea concept lines 62–69 and 151 while keeping the November PAYCO acceptance selector navigation-only.

The May manual `payment_method_types` examples (old raw 43–46, 68–70, 94–97 and 128–145) are dated. In the separate `2026-09-30.endive` Checkout Session and PaymentIntent create documentation, the writable field produces HTTP 400. The Intent error code is `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`. Dynamic payment methods or `allowed_payment_method_types` filter for compatibility and `payment_method_types` remains the computed response field. The Endive endpoint links and REST table establish this scope despite the separate preview label in the Intent Impact paragraph. Generic filtering supplies no PAYCO-specific eligibility (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:5-23; raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36). Keep the dated Direct API Stripe account prerequisite and PaymentIntent amount, `krw`, `payco` type, server-to-client secret handoff, and browser `stripe.confirmPayment` with `return_url`. The May Direct API section explicitly requires the merchant page to show the NICEPAY disclosure and terms link (old raw 115–149 and 218–269).

Keep local processor authentication and authorization, browser return with the PaymentIntent ID and client secret for status verification, and paid status as separate steps. In the dated test redirects, `requires_action` becomes `succeeded` on test authorization or `requires_payment_method` on test failure. Optional post-payment handling uses `payment_intent.succeeded` through Dashboard, webhook or partner integration (old raw 101–103 and 271–298).
conflicts: Source lines 13 and 21 and Korea concept line 66 assert that buyer email and a funding field are unnecessary. Old raw 128–145 and 243–269 omit these inputs in the illustrated PAYCO requests. The May Naver Direct API guide supplies an optional card/points funding setting (raw/stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-158), and the May Kakao payment guide explicitly requires email within Direct API (raw/stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:135-139). source_assessments.reason: The November raw provides navigation. The baseline summary independently requires scope and status corrections that affect how a reader selects a route, completes checkout and interprets the payment result.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-12 identify PAYCO acceptance in South Korea and link Checkout and Direct API. The detailed May 8, 2026 capture describes South Korean customers, 28 merchant locations including Singapore, KRW line items, Checkout payment mode only, and a 100 KRW minimum. The May Checkout guide gives no maximum for card passthrough and sets the stored-value top-up cap at 2,000,000 KRW. It distinguishes dynamic presentation from May manual `payco` enablement (old raw lines 10-46). Direct API first requires a Stripe account (old raw lines 115-119). The server creates a PaymentIntent with amount, `krw` and `payco` in the May method-type list. The browser then calls `stripe.confirmPayment` with that intent’s client secret and a `return_url` (old raw lines 128-149 and 224-269). The merchant page shows the dated NICEPAY disclosure and terms link. The buyer authenticates with the local processor and returns to the merchant. The return carries `payment_intent` and `payment_intent_client_secret` for status verification. In the sandbox, `requires_action` becomes `succeeded` or `requires_payment_method`. The dated guide’s optional business-action path listens for `payment_intent.succeeded` in preference to depending on a client callback (old raw lines 271-298). These test transitions do not establish a live payment. source-stripe-payco-accept-payment.md retains the basic routes but needs these scope and outcome qualifications and more precise treatment of buyer email and funding examples.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-12 are navigation only to the same routes represented in old raw lines 6-8 and 105-107. Keep the May Checkout eligibility, KRW, mode and amount conditions dated. The Stripe-hosted example uses `success_url` and the full embedded example uses `return_url` with `ui_mode: embedded_page` (old raw lines 20-99). In source-stripe-payco-accept-payment.md and the reciprocal Korea concept, PAYCO’s illustrated Direct API requests omit buyer email and a funding selector, while the separate Naver guide documents an optional card/points selector. This example comparison supplies no universal PAYCO field rule (old raw lines 128-145 and 243-269; raw/stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-158). Scope the explicit NICEPAY merchant-page text and terms link to Direct API, and keep local authorization, browser return, verified server payment state and settlement distinct. The archived JavaScript uses `result.error.message` after destructuring `error`; the test states and success event are separate from that sample code (old raw lines 218-298). The separate `2026-07-29.dahlia` changelog adds `payment_method_options.payco.setup_future_usage=none` on applicable Checkout Session and PaymentIntent surfaces to indicate no saving. That field supplies no evidence of reuse, Checkout setup mode or subscription mode. The separate November Korea overview lists PAYCO one-time only (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-samsung-pay-and-payco-setup-future-usage-none-only-2026-11-07.md:5-21; raw/stripe-payments-countries-korea-2026-11-07.md:154-164). Date those statements in the reciprocal Korea route. The separate `2026-09-30.endive` Checkout Session and PaymentIntent create endpoints reject the May writable `payment_method_types` field with HTTP 400. The Intent error code is `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`. Dynamic methods and `allowed_payment_method_types` filter compatibility, and `payment_method_types` stays a computed response field. The versioned links and REST table set the Endive scope despite the Intent Impact paragraph’s different preview label (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:5-23; raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36).
